name: form
why: A symbolic manipulation system from high-energy physics that few developers have ever touched, with a fascinating old-school heritage.

brief.what_it_is: FORM is a symbolic manipulation system. It reads symbolic expressions from program files and applies algebraic transformations to them, such as pattern-matching rewrites on symbols and functions. The answers come back as text in a mathematical notation. Its README stresses that expression size is limited by disk space rather than RAM.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents FORM as a tool that has been essential for many state-of-the-art High Energy Physics computations. Its original author is Jos Vermaseren of NIKHEF, the Dutch institute for subatomic physics.
brief.how_it_works: You write a FORM program in a text file with declarations such as Symbol and CFunction, then a Local expression and rewrite statements such as id ... = ..., and end with Print and .end. The README's examples show a repeat loop that rewrites x^10 into 34 + 55*x, and a pattern that reorders the arguments of f(1,2,x,3,4) to give f(3,4,1,2). The README does not describe the internal mechanism beyond the disk-backed expression size.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the README advises installing optional dependencies gmp, mpfr, zstd, zlib and flint for better performance. Arbitrary-precision floating-point needs both gmp and mpfr; if either is missing that feature is disabled. To build from source, install autoconf and automake, clone the repository, then run autoreconf -i, ./configure, make, make install. The README points to an INSTALL file for advanced options. A precompiled binary is also available from PyPI as form-bin. No accounts or runtime setup are mentioned.
brief.standout: Its landmark feature is that expression size is bounded by disk space instead of RAM, which is unusual for a symbolic algebra tool. The README also describes it as a long-running workhorse in High Energy Physics, with a pattern-matching style built around id statements and a repeat loop.
brief.status: Probably maintained, but the evidence is thin. The GitHub README links to release notes for FORM 5.0, a stable online manual, and a test CI badge, and it invites issues and discussions. I did not see a release date or last-commit date, so I cannot confirm the timing. The fetched GitHub URL (vermaseren/form) served the form-dev/form README.
brief.caveats: The homepage https://www.nikhef.nl/~form/ was unreachable (URLError), so the entry relies on the GitHub README. The brew description is 'Symbolic manipulation system', which matches the README. Build from source needs autoconf and automake, and the optional libraries make arbitrary-precision float support depend on gmp and mpfr. Licensing is in a COPYING file that I did not read. The scout note's claim that few developers have touched it is not from the README and is not included here.
quotes: FORM is a Symbolic Manipulation System. It reads symbolic expressions from files and executes symbolic/algebraic transformations upon them.
As its landmark feature, the size of the considered expressions in FORM is only limited by the available disk space and not by the available RAM.
FORM has been essential for many state-of-the-art computations in High Energy Physics.
